subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Subaru WRX STI
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Subaru WRX STI.

hook.text: Subaru was a tiny maker of boring economy cars—until rally racing changed everything.

buildup.text: In the 1990s, Subaru entered the World Rally Championship with turbocharged all-wheel-drive sedans.

discovery.text: The WRX STI brought that rally technology to the street—turbo flat-four, AWD, and aggressive styling.

twist.text: It cost under $30,000 when competitors like the Mitsubishi Evo were its only real rival.

climax.text: The STI built a cult following. Subaru went from obscure to beloved among driving enthusiasts.

punchline.text: Rally bred a street legend on a budget.

quiz.question: What motorsport made the WRX STI famous?

details.summary: The Subaru WRX STI brought World Rally Championship technology to the street, combining a turbocharged boxer engine with symmetrical all-wheel drive to create an affordable rally car for public roads.
details.whyItMatters: The WRX STI proved that rally success translates directly to showroom appeal. It created a devoted enthusiast community and made all-wheel-drive performance accessible to everyday buyers.
takeaways: Its boxer engine and symmetrical AWD were born in rally racing
The turbocharged flat-four delivered over 300 HP in later models
Its rivalry with the Mitsubishi Evo defined performance car culture in the 2000s

faq.question: What makes the WRX STI's all-wheel drive special?
faq.answer: Subaru's symmetrical AWD system places the drivetrain along the car's center line for balanced weight distribution. The STI adds a driver-controlled center differential that varies front-to-rear torque split.

faq.question: Why did Subaru discontinue the STI?
faq.answer: Stricter emissions regulations and the shift toward electrification made the high-revving turbocharged engine difficult to justify. Subaru has hinted at an electrified performance variant as a future successor.
